scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8155: We cannot reach anything on Campus 1 from the rest
of the network this morning -- none of the 172.16.10.x / 172.16.20.x /
172.16.30.x machines answer from over here, while the Campus 1 people say
everything works inside their own building. So the break is whatever joins
Campus 1 to the rest, and operations already named it when we rang: "their
edge box has probably died again" -- the one called "router16". I won't
pretend to know what that is, but it is your box. Check it and bring
Campus 1 back today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router16 is up: it holds its OSPF adjacencies
  (the mswitch0 uplink and the router7 link are Full), it has dynamic routes, and
  it forwards Campus 1 traffic to the rest of the network. A Campus 1 host reaches
  a Campus 2 host (e.g. 10.5.0.254) through router16 with 0% loss. The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a core-router
  outage that is not occurring (cf. kath4-router16-ospfd-down, where router16's
  ospfd IS down).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- router16 down, Campus 1
cut off -- is NOT reproducible: router16 is up with full OSPF neighbors (mswitch0
uplink and the router7 link in Full state), it has dynamic routes, and a Campus 1
host reaches Campus 2 (10.5.0.254) through router16 with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: router16 is healthy and forwarding,
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces a Campus
1 -> off-campus path through router16, finds it working, checks router16's OSPF
neighbors and that it is forwarding, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds"
a dead core router -- restarting router16 or blaming it to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** None — no subsystem, interface, daemon, or policy is misconfigured or failed in the live network.

**Mechanism:** The helpdesk ticket describes an inter-campus reachability outage (172.16.10.x / 172.16.20.x / 172.16.30.x unreachable from the rest of the network), with router16 named as the suspect edge device. A full four-phase diagnostic sweep of the live Kath4 topology finds no evidence of this fault.

**Localization:** Phase 1 reachability shows 0 % packet loss on all 28 tested host-to-host paths, explicitly including cross-campus probes from the 10.5.0.x and 10.6.0.x segments to all three Campus 1 subnets. Phase A infrastructure sweep (28 devices) finds zero ACL drop rules, zero static-ARP anomalies, and all 15 end hosts correctly addressed with default routes. Phase B OSPF snapshot confirms every one of the 9 FRR routers — including router16 — has its ospfd daemon active, vtysh accessible, and all adjacencies in Full state; router16 specifically holds 2 Full OSPF neighbours (bond0 toward mswitch0, eth2 toward router7) and carries the full 18-route table. The three Campus 1 subnets (172.16.10.0/24, 172.16.20.0/24, 172.16.30.0/24) are advertised by mswitch0 and present in every router's table. Traffic-control sweep confirms zero shaping or corruption qdiscs. Phase D pressure sweep finds zero stressed or resource-saturated devices.

**Root cause:** The reported outage is not reproducible in the current live network state; either the incident was transient and has self-recovered, or the symptom was misattributed to this topology.

**Fix:** No corrective action is required. Continue monitoring router16's OSPF adjacency and bond0 interface for future instability; if the fault recurs, capture `show ip ospf neighbor` and interface counters on router16 and mswitch0 at the time of the outage.

The writeup accurately reflects the logged outputs and appropriately concludes no reproducible fault.
